'''Manoug Manougian''' (April 29, 1935 – March 27, 2024) was an Armenian scientist and academic who was considered to be the father of the [[Lebanese space program]]. Manougian was born on April 29, 1935, in Jerusalem. He died on March 27, 2024, in Tampa, Florida. He came to the United States in 1956. His parents are Nishan and Sirpouhi Manougian.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://archive.aramcoworld.com/issue/201303/the.forgotten.apogee.of.lebanese.rocketry.htm |title=The Forgotten Apogee of Lebanese Rocketry|publisher=Saudi Aramco World|author=Sheldon Chad|access-date=March 11, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://thepolitic.org/article/an-interview-with-dr-manoug-manougian-former-leader-of-the-lebanese-rocket-society |title=An Interview with Dr. Manoug Manougian, Former Leader of the Lebanese Rocket Society|author=Mehr Nadeem|date=March 29, 2017|website=thepolitic.org|access-date=March 11, 2023}}</ref>

== Background ==
Manougian grew up in [[Jerusalem]] and was educated at [[St. George's School, Jerusalem]].
Manougian won a scholarship to the [[University of Texas]], and he graduated in 1960 with a major in math.<ref name="telegraph">{{cite web|title=The Lebanese Rocket Society - The Telegraph review (14/10/2013)|publisher=The Telegraph|url=http://www.abboutproductions.com/specificNewsA?id=119|author=Alex Hannaford|access-date=March 11, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230311204245/http://www.abboutproductions.com/specificNewsA?id=119|archive-date=March 11, 2023|url-status=dead}}</ref> Right away, Haigazian College in [[Beirut]] was glad to offer him a job teaching both math and physics. The college also made him the faculty advisor for the science club.
Manougian met his wife in Armenia {{circa|1955}} when he became her tutor. They eloped shortly after to the United States. While his wife attended school in Ohio, Manougian attended the University of Texas (see above). After graduating, they moved to Beirut.<ref name="telegraph"/>

Manougian died on March 27, 2024, at the age of 88.<ref>{{cite web |title=Manoug Manougian Professor Emeritus In Memoriam |url=https://www.usf.edu/arts-sciences/departments/mathematics-statistics/people/faculty/manoug-manougian.aspx |website=University of South Florida |access-date=22 January 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Dr. Manoug Manougian: The passing of a pioneer. A lasting legacy! |url=https://www.haigazian.edu.lb/2024/05/07/dr-manoug-manougian-the-passing-of-a-pioneer-a-lasting-legacy/ |access-date=22 March 2025 |publisher=Haigazian University |date=7 May 2024}}</ref>

== Career ==
Manougian married in 1960 and went to Lebanon to become a teacher at [[Haigazian College]].<ref>{{cite web|title=The Bizarre Tale of the Middle East's First Space Program|author=Peter Schwartzstein
|date=October 17, 2016|url=https://www.smithsonianmag.com/history/bizarre-tale-middle-easts-first-space-program-180960808/|publisher=Smithsonian Magazine|access-date=March 11, 2023}}</ref>

=== Lebanese space program ===
Manougian founded the Haigazian College Rocket Society in November 1960.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/magazine-24735423 |title=Lebanon's forgotten space programme|publisher=BBC News|author=Richard Hooper|date= November 14, 2013|access-date=March 11, 2023}}</ref> With a very limited budget, the society launched a series of rockets to increasing altitudes.  It received funding from the Lebanese government and became the [[Lebanese Rocket Society]].  He and his students finally launched a [[suborbital rocket]] in 1963. The [[Cedar rocket|Cedar IV rocket]], launched on Lebanese independence day, 21 November 1963 from [[Dbayeh]] north of Beirut, reached {{convert|90|mi}} and was featured on Lebanese stamps.<ref>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101204114602/http://www.haigazian.edu.lb/About%20HU/Pages/HU1stRocket.aspx |archive-date=4 December 2010|title=HU produced the 1st rockets shot in the Arab world |author1=Gorune Assarian|author2=Virginie Daldalian|url=http://www.haigazian.edu.lb/About%20HU/Pages/HU1stRocket.aspx|publisher=Haigazian University}}</ref>

=== Teaching ===
Manougian returned to the United States in 1966.  Manougian completed a master's degree and doctorate at the University of Texas and continued his academic career in the Department of Mathematics at the [[University of South Florida]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Department of Mathematics - Dr. Manoug N. Manougian|url=http://shell.cas.usf.edu/math/People/Faculty/manougian.html|website=University of South Florida|access-date=March 11, 2023}}</ref> He was an adviser for the University's Society of Aeronautics and Rocketry which is currently trying to launch to rocket above the [[kármán line]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Spata |first1=Christopher |title=USF's rocket club is an underdog. Can it win a $1 million space race? |url=https://www.tampabay.com/arts-entertainment/2020/01/15/usfs-rocket-club-is-an-underdog-can-it-win-a-1-million-space-race/ |accessdate=23 February 2020 |work=Tampa Bay Times |date=15 January 2020 |language=en}}</ref>

== Views and politics ==
As a member of the Armenian diaspora, he has been known to write editorials advocating awareness about the [[Armenian genocide]]. He is also a co-author and associate producer of a 4-hour documentary called ''The Genocide Factor: The Human Tragedy'', that aired on [[PBS]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.usforacle.com/2010/10/19/an-address-to-armenia/|title=An address to Armenia|author=Brenda Medina|publisher=The Oracle|date=October 19, 2010|access-date=March 11, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160509115640/http://www.tbo.com/list/news-opinion-commentary/manoug-manougian-lesson-ignored-the-armenian-genocide-20150415/|archive-date=May 9, 2016 |url=http://www.tbo.com/list/news-opinion-commentary/manoug-manougian-lesson-ignored-the-armenian-genocide-20150415/|title=Lesson ignored: the Armenian Genocide|publisher=The Tampa Tribune|date=April 15, 2015}}</ref>  In addition, he vehemently believes that rocketry and science should be pursued for solely peaceful means.<ref name="telegraph"/> Consequentially, he turned down multiple lucrative offers during his time in the Lebanese Rocket Society rather than let his work be used for military purposes.
